extracted.intended_audience: Federal agencies, agency counsel, HR specialists, employee relations practitioners, and stakeholders participating in OPM rulemaking/notice-and-comment
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and regulatory clarifications in OPM's final rule addressing movement to/within the excepted service, adverse action procedures, and related definitions and appeal rights under title 5. Includes guidance on regulatory conformity with statute and precedent, implementation costs, and expected impacts on recruitment and retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of accrued status and civil service protections on involuntary moves
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee who is moved involuntarily from the competitive service to an excepted service position, or from one excepted service schedule to another, retains the status and civil service protections the employee had already accrued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM makes plain this retention of accrued rights; the regulation clarifies that such moves do not strip employees of previously-earned procedural and appeal rights. The rule also adds related guardrails and (narrow) appeal rights (see 5 CFR 302.603) to protect against agencies asserting loss of status. This alignment prevents improper terminations and confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'confidential, policy-determining, policy-making, or policy-advocating' positions
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule explicitly defines these terms to mean a noncareer political appointment identified by a close working relationship with the President, head of an agency, or other key appointed officials, directly responsible for furthering the President's goals and policies and carrying no expectation of continued employment beyond the presidential administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM added definitions to align regulations with statutory text, congressional intent, legislative history, legal precedent, and longstanding OPM practice. The clarity is intended to identify employees/positions excluded from civil service protections and to reduce agency confusion about coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum requirements for moving employees into and within the excepted service (5 CFR 302.602)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule establishes minimum procedural requirements agencies must follow when moving employees and positions into and within the excepted service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These requirements create guardrails to protect existing rights and reinforce merit system principles. Agencies must follow the procedures to avoid improperly depriving employees of status or protections; the guidance aligns these requirements with existing excepted service regulations (schedules D and E) and OPM reporting obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrow MSPB appeal right for contested involuntary moves (5 CFR 302.603)
rubrics_metrics.description: OPM confers a narrow appeal right to the Merit Systems Protection Board (MSPB) for employees whose positions are placed involuntarily into the excepted service, or excepted service employees moved involuntarily between schedules, where an agency asserts the employee loses status or accrued protections in violation of the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM considered but rejected alternatives (e.g., relying solely on EEO, OSC, administrative grievances, or negotiated grievance procedures). The new appeal right provides earlier recourse following an involuntary movement and helps protect employee status and morale; it is limited in scope to such claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformity of part 752 with statute and Federal Circuit precedent
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to 5 CFR part 752 (adverse actions) are made to conform to statutory language and Federal Circuit caselaw, including clarifications for suspensions, removals, and furloughs and to close regulatory gaps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM revised subpart D to reflect Federal Circuit interpretation of 5 U.S.C. 7511 and elected previously not to update subpart B for suspensions of 14 days or less; the current rule closes gaps to reduce confusion that can lead to improper terminations, reversed MSPB decisions, and wasted resources. Agencies should rely on the updated regulation rather than outdated text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on OPM authority to remove adverse action rights
rubrics_metrics.description: OPM states it is not authorized to remove adverse action rights from broad categories of career civil servants; elimination of such protections can be done only by congressional enactment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a legal constraint on regulatory action—OPM cannot strip statutory protections by regulation even if commenters argue for it. Comments asserting otherwise lack basis in OPM's regulatory authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural protections for tenured employees and due process considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural protections enacted by Congress provide tenured employees an adequate opportunity to be heard and to explore facts and law before adverse actions are taken; where Congress has created a property interest, due process protects employees from unlawful deprivation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM emphasizes that procedural protections apply broadly (not only to problem employees) and are necessary to maintain a merit-based civil service; such protections are characterized as a small price to pay for avoiding political patronage and protecting public confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of chapter 75 procedures for many performance-based adverse actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Supervisors can and do use chapter 75 (adverse actions) rather than chapter 43 for suspending, demoting, or removing employees with unacceptable performance; in a chapter 75 proceeding the supervisor need only disclose grounds, provide supporting evidence, and show that the action will promote the efficiency of the service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no statutory requirement under chapter 75 to allow the employee a period to improve performance before proposing action. This clarifies expectations and remedies available to supervisors and agencies managing performance issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to update agency policies/procedures to comply with the final regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must update internal policies and procedures to ensure compliance with amended provisions of 5 CFR (listed parts include 210.102(b), 212.401, 213.3301, 302.101, 302.602, 302.603, 451.302, and amendments to parts 432 and 752).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM provides cost estimates for agency implementation (assumptions about staff GS-14 step 5 rates, hours for first-year and ongoing work, and governmentwide totals). Agencies should budget for policy updates and potential appeal resolution under section 302.603.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory clarity to prevent inadvertent reliance on out-of-date rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Retaining outdated information in Government regulations can confuse agencies, managers, and employees and produce unintended outcomes (e.g., failure to notify employees of appeal rights, use of improper procedures leading to reversals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM updates regulations to align with precedent and statute to mitigate errors in personnel actions. Clear, current regulations help HR specialists and managers avoid mistakes and ensure employees receive proper notice of rights and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of recruitment, hiring, and retention impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: The rulemaking should be assessed for its effects on agencies' ability to recruit, hire, and retain talent; preserving civil service protections promotes merit system principles, job stability, and attractiveness of federal employment compared to private sector alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM finds that weakening protections risks politicization, higher turnover, loss of institutional knowledge, and difficulty filling technical positions (e.g., auditors, economists, IT, cybersecurity). Comments and empirical evidence about recruitment/retention (especially in scientific and technical roles) informed the agency's assessment of benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance and applicability of evidence cited in comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence submitted by commenters should be relevant to the U.S. federal civil service; studies of European private-sector labor markets or state at-will systems do not demonstrate effects on American federal civil service protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM rejects arguments based on foreign or inapplicable state contexts when they do not show how removing protections would affect U.S. career civil servants. Commenters should provide U.S.-relevant, civil-service-specific evidence to support regulatory change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitations: proposals outside the rulemaking or OPM authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggestions such as curbing burrowing in, capping Schedule C appointments, scrutinizing SES appointments, changing hiring preferences, adding whistleblower protections, revising RIF assignment rights, modifying probationary periods, reforming chapters 43/75, or pushing policies into collective bargaining are outside the scope of this rulemaking and/or OPM regulatory authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM acknowledges these suggestions but found them outside scope or authority and therefore did not adopt them in this rule. Stakeholders should raise such proposals through appropriate statutory or separate regulatory processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPM's 'least burdensome' implementation standard
rubrics_metrics.description: OPM asserts that the regulations are issued in the least burdensome way possible and do not impose new substantive requirements beyond existing statutes, regulations, and case law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM expects negligible operational impact for covered agencies, aligning procedural requirements for excepted service moves with existing OPM regulations for other excepted schedules and reporting obligations.
